title: Mixed Economy
author: oA7a2DXCeN3DLamvj
chapter_outcomes: Explain the purpose and nature of business activity, including needs, wants, scarcity, opportunity cost, importance of specialisation, and the concept of adding value.
Describe the primary, secondary, and tertiary economic sectors, their classification, and reasons for changes in their importance.
Classify business enterprises between private sector and public sector in a mixed economy
Explain enterprise and entrepreneurship, including characteristics of successful entrepreneurs, contents of a business plan, and government support for start-ups (e.g. grants, training schemes)
Explain methods of measuring business size, including number of employees, output, and capital employed, and evaluate their limitations.
Explain why some businesses grow while others remain small, the ways of growth, associated problems, and possible solutions.
Explain causes of business failure and why new businesses are at greater risk.

Describe the main features of different forms of business organisation, including sole traders, partnerships, private and public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures, and public sector organisations; explain differences between unincorporated businesses and limited companies; discuss risk, ownership, and limited liability; and recommend and justify a suitable form of business organisation in a given situation.
Explain the need for business objectives, types of objectives (survival, growth, profit, market share), and objectives of social enterprises.
Explain the role of internal and external stakeholders, their objectives, and how conflicts between them may arise.
Differences in the objectives of private sector and public sector enterprises
